added: #Choose an under-cabinet lighting kit. There are many different types of light to consider. You can choose from LED,  fluorescent, incandescent, halogen or Xenon lights.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Find your source of power. The lighting will require a power source. Plan how you will run cable to the lighting/fixture locations. Determine if you are prepared to run wires, cut holes into the wall, and create new electrical boxes. Alternatively, consider plugging the light fixture into existing outlets or finding battery powered lighting. Plugging in the lighting into an existing outlet means you have to decide how to camouflage the lighting’s power cable.<ref>http://www.electrical-online.com/installing-under-cabinet-lighting</ref>[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Determine your layout. Lay your light on the countertop, underneath where you plan to do the installation. If you plan to run multiple lights, find lights that have a quick-connect cord. This cord will connect lights using only one power source.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 3 Version 3.jpg|center]]
[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Determine if you need a new electrical box. If you plan to add new wires or a light switches that to an existing kitchen outlet, make sure the electrical box that houses the outlet has enough room. You will have to replace the box with a larger one if it doesn’t.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Turn off the power to the kitchen. Do this at the circuit breaker. Find the switch labeled kitchen and make sure it’s off. Test to see if the power is turned off, plug in a device such as a lamp or radio into the outlet and see if it turns on.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Remove the outlet from the electrical box. First, unscrew the wall plate that holds the outlet. Then, unscrew the outlet from the electrical box. Take the outlet out and disconnect any wires that are connected to it.<ref>http://homeguides.sfgate.com/hardwire-install-undercabinet-led-lights-65128.html</ref>[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Draw an outline of the new electrical box. Hold the new electrical box over the existing box in the wall so the expansion of the hole is on the side that isn’t nailed to a stud. Use a pencil to make an outline of where you will cut with the drywall saw.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#Enlarge the hole. Use a drywall saw to cut along the tracing you made. Make sure you’re not hitting any studs.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]
[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 10 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Find the knockout in the back of the light fixture. A knockout is a pre-scored hole made to run wire easily without drilling extra holes.<ref>http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/how-to/step/0,,20217311_826147,00.html</ref>[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 11 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Take out the knockout plug or plate. There might be a plug or plate in the fixture’s knockout hole. Use a screwdriver to either pry the plug loose or unscrew the plate.<ref>http://homeguides.sfgate.com/hardwire-install-undercabinet-led-lights-65128.html</ref>[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 12 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Plan where you will drill. Before drilling a hole in the wall so that you can run cables, you need to plot the spot. Place the light fixture in the exact location you plan to install it. Find the spot on the wall directly across from the light fixture’s knockout hole. Draw an “X” on this spot using a pencil.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 13 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#Drill a hole into the “X.” The hole needs to be just big enough to run the cable, so it’s best to use a ½-inch spade bit.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 14 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Cut your cable. Measure the distance between the electrical box and the hole you drilled. Take the distance you measured and add 24 to the length. This is how much of the 12/2 nonmetallic cable you need to cut. Adding the length to measure gives the cable some slack when you run it through the wall.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 15 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Run the cable into the hole you drilled. Go to the hole where the electrical box was and reach into the wall. Grab the cable hanging from the small hole you drilled. Once you have the cable, pull it through the electrical box hole.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 16 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Take off the cover and socket strip on the light fixture. Take off everything until you have just the casing of the light fixture. Clearing the fixture will give you space to screw the fixture into the cabinets.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 17 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Place the light fixture. Put the fixture where you plan to install it. Make sure it is lined with the edge of the cabinet or behind it.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 18 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#Attach the light fixture to the cabinet. Screw the fixture to the cabinet using the screws the manufacturer provided in the kit.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 19 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Place a cable clamp in the fixture’s knockout hole. Insert a ½-inch nonmetallic cable clamp in the fixture’s knockout hole to hold the cable in place and protect it from damage. Unscrew the plate that locks the clamp and place the clamp in the knockout hole. Once the clamp is in place, screw the plate back into it from the outside of the fixture.<ref>http://homeguides.sfgate.com/hardwire-install-undercabinet-led-lights-65128.html</ref>[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 20 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Run the cable into the fixture. Grab the cable hanging from the small hole in the wall and run it into the knockout hole of the fixture.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 21 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Strip the cable. Use a wire stripper to remove the coating around the end of the cable that's in the fixture. Once stripped, connect the exposed wires to the corresponding wires in the light fixture: black-to-black, white-to-white, and bare copper to green. Do this by twisting orange wire connectors to the ends of the wires.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 22 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Reattach the cover and socket strip on the light fixture. Make sure all the connections are secure and that there is no exposed wired. Once you reattach everything back to the light fixture, staple the cable to the cabinet using cable staples.<ref>http://homeguides.sfgate.com/hardwire-install-undercabinet-led-lights-65128.html</ref>[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 23 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#Place the light bulbs you selected into the socket strip on the fixture.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 24 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Run the cables into the new electrical box. There will be two sets of cables: the cable that ran into the old electrical box and the cable you ran from the light fixture. Pull both cables through the new electrical box.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 25 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Place the electrical box into the hole you created in the drywall. The fins on the outside of the box should rest firmly against the wall so that you can screw it in securely.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 26 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Screw the electrical box into the wall. The box has fins that flip inside the wall when you screw it. Make sure you feel the fins flip as these secure the box to the wall.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 27 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Use a GFCI outlet. A ground fault circuit interrupter outlet will help prevent dangerous shocks that could seriously injure or kill someone.<ref>http://www.leviton.com/OA_HTML/SectionDisplay.jsp?section=37683</ref>[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 28 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Connect the wires from the new outlet to the cables in the electrical box. Use wire strippers to remove the insulation on the cables. Once the wires are exposed, strip on the insulation on them as well. Connect the corresponding wires using an orange wire connector. Use a green pigtail connector to combine the copper wires from both cables and the outlet. <ref>http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/how-to/step/0,,20217311_826157,00.html</ref>[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 29 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Screw the white and black wire into the GFCI outlet. Make sure you combine the black and white wires from both cables and the outlet. Once they are combined, screw the free end of each of these wires into the corresponding terminal on the outlet. These terminals will be labeled “hot-wire line” and “white-wire line.”[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 30 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Connect the dimmer or light switch. If you are installing a light switch into the outlet, connect the yellow wire from the switch to a black wire coming from the light fixture cable. Attach the copper wire from the switch to the copper wire on the GFCI outlet. Connect the white wires together. Make sure you use cable connectors to combine all wires.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 31 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Tuck in the wires. Once everything is connected, carefully pack the wires into the electrical box. Screw the outlet and switch to the electrical box.[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 32 Version 2.jpg|center]]

Determine if you are prepared to run wires, cut holes into the wall, and create new electrical boxes. #*Consider hiring an electrician if you’re uncomfortable tieing the lighting to any electrical wiring.<ref>http://www.familyhandyman.com/kitchen/diy-kitchen-cabinets/how-to-install-under-cabinet-lighting-in-your-kitchen/view-all</ref>
#*Make sure you are using a code-compliant source of electricity.
#*Make sure the source of power you selected isn’t dedicated to the refrigerator or any other kitchen appliances. You don’t want to overload the circuit.

#Determine your layout. Lay your light on the countertop, underneath where you plan to do the installation. If you plan to run multiple lights, find lights that have a quick-connect cord. This cord will connect lights using only one power source.

#*Most installations are usually above the sink, work areas, and small appliances.<ref>http://images.lowes.com/videos/DITV/0907/pdfs/404--How%20to%20Install%20Low-Voltage%20Under-Cabinet%20Lighting.pdf</ref>
#*For the best lighting, place the lights as close as possible to the front of the cabinet.
#*Some manufacturers suggest that multiple lights be at least 12 inches apart.

#Clear your workspace. Make sure the cabinets and counters are free from anything that might get in your way while working. If you need to go through your cabinets for wiring, make sure all the items are removed.
===Part 2: Preparing the Power===

#Determine if you need a new electrical box. If you add new wires that connect with the outlet from the lighting, make sure the box that houses the outlet has enough room. You will have to replace the box with a larger one if it doesn’t.

#*To figure the minimum box size required by the National Electrical Code, add 1 for each hot and neutral wire entering the box, 1 for all the ground wires combined, 1 for all the clamps combined, and 2 for each device (switch or receptacle, but usually not light fixtures) installed in the box. Multiply this figure by 2 for 14-gauge wire and 2.25 for 12-gauge wire to get the minimum box volume in cubic inches. Plastic boxes have the volume stamped inside. <ref>http://www.familyhandyman.com/kitchen/diy-kitchen-cabinets/how-to-install-under-cabinet-lighting-in-your-kitchen/view-all</ref>
#Turn off the electricity to the kitchen at the main electrical panel. To be sure the power is off, plug in a lamp and make sure it doesn't light.

#Pull the outlet from the electrical box. Unscrew the wall plate. Loosen the screws on the outlet and pull the wires from beneath them to release the outlet from the electrical box in the wall.<ref>http://homeguides.sfgate.com/hardwire-install-undercabinet-led-lights-65128.html</ref>
#*The electrical box is nailed to a wall stud. Find out which stud by peeking between the sides of the box and the drywall.

#Trace the outline of the new electrical box. Hold a two-gang, old-work electrical box over the existing box in the wall so the expansion of the hole is on the side that isn’t nailed to a stud. Trace around it with a pencil.
#*This larger box replaces the existing single-gang receptacle box in the wall. An "old work" box is for remodeling. It has fins that unfold behind the drywall to lock it in place.
#Enlarge the hole. Use a drywall saw to cut along the tracing you made. Make sure you’re not hitting any studs.
#Remove the old electrical box. After enlarging the hole, make sure the cable coming into the electrical box is loose, then use a flat pry bar to remove it.
===Part 3: Running Cable===

#Hold the light fixture in place and locate the knockout in the back. A knockout is a prescored hole made to easily run wire without drilling extra holes.<ref>http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/how-to/step/0,,20217311_826147,00.html</ref>

#Mark the wall straight across from the knockout in lighting fixture. Use a stud finder to see if there's a wall stud between the mark and the hole for the electrical box. If so, move your mark to the other side of the stud.
#Use a ½-inch-diameter spade bit to drill through the wall directly below the upper wall cabinet. This will be where you marked the wall.
#Cut a length of 12/2 NM (nonmetallic) electrical cable long enough to reach from the ½-inch hole to the two-gang box hole. Add an extra 24 inches to the length.

#Feed one end of the cable into the ½-inch hole bored in the upper backsplash wall. Gently reach into the hole where the electrical box will be installed, grab the cable end, and pull it through into the kitchen.
===Part 4: Installing the Light Fixture===
#Remove the cover and the metal socket strip that holds the bulbs from the light fixture. This is so you have room to work.
#Hold the fixture against the underside of the cabinet, then slide it forward until it's hidden behind the cabinet's front edge.
#Screw it to the cabinet with the screws provided.
#Use a slotted screwdriver to pry the round knockout plug from the rear of the light fixture.
#Install a cable connector in the fixture’s knockout hole.  This will hold the cable in place and protect it from the fixture’s sharp edges. This provides additional safety and prevents damage.
#Strip away 6 inches of the outer plastic sheathing from the end of the cable.
#Feed the cable through the connector.
#Tighten the connector screws to secure the cable. Be sure the connector clamps down on the cable's plastic sheathing, not the individual wires.
===Part 6: Installing the Electrical Box===
#Hold the new, two-gang electrical box close to the hole you cut in the backsplash wall.
#Feed the end of the existing cable — the one that was attached to the receptacle — into the two-gang box.
#Pull the end of the cable coming from the light fixture into the box. Push the box into the hole and press it tightly against the wall.

#Tighten the screws on the new electrical box. Note that the box has two screws, one in each diagonal corner. As you begin to tighten the screws, the box's plastic fins will flip up behind the drywall. Continue to tighten the screws until you feel the fins pull tight against the rear of the drywall, locking the box in place.
#*Before sliding the two-gang box in the wall, test it to make sure the fins pop up.
===Part 7: Attaching the Outlet===

#Use a GFCI outlet. A  ground fault circuit interrupter outlet. These outlets are designed to reduce the occurrences of serious injury or death associated with electrical accidents.<ref>http://www.leviton.com/OA_HTML/SectionDisplay.jsp?section=37683</ref>
#*Once installed, this outlet’s ground-fault circuit interrupter will shut off instantaneously if you are electrocuted.
#Join the bare copper grounding wires from both the existing and new cable with a green pigtail connector.

#Cut off the remaining cable, separate the white wire, and cut two 8-inch-long pieces. Strip a 1/2-inch of insulation off their ends and join them to both white wires in the box with a wire connector.
#Fasten the other end of one of the 8-inch white wires to the silver GFCI screw terminal marked "white-wire line."
#Cut two 8-inch-long black wires, strip off ½ inch of insulation, and join them to the black wire coming from the existing (receptacle) cable.
#Fasten the free end of one of these wires to "hot-wire line" GFCI terminal.
#Wrap the pigtail around the green grounding screw on the GFCI, leaving at least 4 inches of wire sticking out beyond the screw.
#Peel the plastic sheathing with lineman's pliers before screwing on wire connectors.
===Part 9: Finalizing the Fixture and Wall plate===
#Reinstall the socket strip in the fixture, but don't put the bulbs in place just yet.

#Inside each fixture is a white, black,and green wire. Connect them to the wires of the same color coming from the cable, using wire connectors: black to black, white to white, and bare copper to green.
#Add the bulbs to the socket strip and install the cover on the fixture.
#Screw on the two-gang wall plate.
#Turn the power back on and test your work.
==What you Need==
*Flat Pry bar to remove old electrical box
*Phillips and slotted Screwdrivers
*Drywall saw to cut the hold for the new electrical box
*1/2 spade bit to bore a hole in the wall for the new cable
*Wire Strippers, to remove insulation from wires
*Lineman’s pliers, to cut and twist together wires
*Drill/driver to drive screws and bore holes
*GFCI receptacle
*Two-gang, old-work electrical box
*Two-gang wall plate
*6 feet of 12/2 NM (nonmetallic) electrical cable plastic-sheathed cable.
*Ground pigtail connector
*Cable connector
*Wire connectors

Cut more holes in the studs along the underside of the cabinet. You will need to string cable out to the further fixture, so make sure to cut enough holes.

#Connect a cable to the power source.

[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 6.jpg|center|550px]]
#* Install a cable clamp to the fixture box and run your new cable to it.

#Feed the cable.

[[Image:Install Under Cabinet Lighting Step 7.jpg|center|550px]]
#* Use fish tape to pull the cable from the fixture box to your newly cut switch.
